exercises.name: Easy Walk
exercises.note: Do not sit down yet. After a match your heart rate is still high and there is adrenaline in your system, and trying to go straight to stillness does not work. Give it five minutes of easy movement first and the rest of this session will actually land.

good: Slow walk, anywhere. Around the court is fine
Let your breathing come down on its own. Do not try to control it yet
bad: Sitting straight down with your bag
Replaying points while you walk. That comes later, not now

good: Relaxed and loose, let the arm swing across and open
Let the upper back turn with it
bad: Forcing the end range. Nothing here is a stretch you fight

good: Slow, one vertebra at a time, breathe with it
Out as you round, in as you arch

exercises.name: Legs Up the Wall
exercises.note: Heavy legs after a long match are partly blood and fluid sitting in them. Getting your feet above your heart for a few minutes helps that drain. It is also the easiest position in the world to breathe in, which is why it comes before the breathing rather than after.

good: On your back, heels resting up the wall, arms out wide
Nothing to hold. Let the legs be heavy and the floor take you
Knees wide, hips back to the heels, arms long
Breathe into your back and feel it widen
bad: Rushing to get to the breathing

exercises.name: Box Breathing
exercises.note: Box breathing comes first here for a reason. Straight after competition your head is still going over points and the counting gives it something to hold on to. Trying to just relax with a racing mind rarely works. Corral the attention first, then drop.

good: All four counts equal. In for four, hold four, out for four, hold four
Through the nose the whole way if you can
Shorten to three if four is a fight. The count matters less than the rhythm
bad: Straining to hold. If you are gasping on the next inhale, the count is too long
Speeding up as you get bored

exercises.name: Extended Exhale Breathing
exercises.note: The long exhale is the part that does the work. A longer out-breath than in-breath is what tips you towards the recovery side of your nervous system. Everything before this session was getting you into a position and a state where this actually works.

good: In through the nose for four, out through the mouth for eight
One hand on your chest, one on your belly. Only the belly hand should move
Let the shoulders drop on every single exhale
bad: Rushing the exhale to get to the next breath
Breathing high into the chest and shoulders
